metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >-15% from prior 5-day avg), model often fails to adjust; add 10–15% downward bias in next 3–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- Model overestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 10–15 days.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +0.5+), model often delays correction; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, model tends to lag; add 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days if sentiment is positive.  
- Model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven markets; if sentiment swings >0.5 in 3 days, increase forecast variance by 10–15% for next 5–7 days.
